system.name: Pi
system.description: A minimal, extensible agent harness: the `pi` command-line coding agent, which works on files in a folder with a model, and the libraries it ships.

corpus.included: The whole repository at this revision with its history, read only: packages/coding-agent, agent, ai, tui, mcp, codemode, schema, telemetry and evals, the root documents and config files, .github, .pi, scripts and nix. Dependencies, generated output and secrets are left out.
corpus.excluded: apps/p2, apps/p2-mac, apps/p3, packages/chord, packages/durable and packages/env: an experimental product line (the Pi Durable runtime and the apps built on it; apps/p2's README calls it a prototype that will be gone soon), which the `pi` CLI and its libraries do not depend on.

consumers.name: Pi user
consumers.description: A person who runs `pi` in a working folder to get a task done with a model, and who sets Pi up for their work.

consumers.name: Extension author
consumers.description: A developer who writes TypeScript extensions and Pi packages that run inside Pi to add tools, commands, providers and interface.

consumers.name: Integrator
consumers.description: Another program that runs Pi's agent, in process through the SDK or as a child process over RPC or the JSON event stream, such as an editor plugin or a chat bot.

consumers.name: Library developer
consumers.description: A developer who builds their own application from Pi's published libraries without using the coding agent.

providers.name: Pi
providers.description: The `pi` coding agent: it runs a model in a working folder with tools, keeps the conversations as sessions, and loads the user's packages, extensions, skills and settings.

parts.name: Settings store
parts.why: Storage of the user's and project's preferences (src/core/settings-manager.ts) that every part reads; writes go through its setters and decide nothing.

parts.name: Terminal UI
parts.why: The interactive mode and its themes and keybindings (src/modes/interactive, src/core/keybindings.ts), drawn with the Pi TUI library: a client that presents the session, part of the terminal UI interface.

parts.name: Print mode, JSON event stream and RPC mode
parts.why: I/O layers over the agent session (src/modes/print-mode.ts, json-event.ts, rpc/): parts of their interfaces; RpcClient is a client of RPC mode.

parts.name: Shell commands
parts.why: Argument parsing and the install, auth, mcp and config commands (src/main.ts, src/cli/, src/package-manager-cli.ts, src/extensions/mcp/cli.ts): part of the pi shell commands interface; they call the components.

parts.name: SDK exports
parts.why: src/index.ts re-exports the session factory, contracts and tool factories: part of the SDK interface.

parts.name: Pi TUI, Pi MCP and Pi Codemode libraries
parts.why: Libraries Pi bundles: the renderer of the terminal UI, the adapter MCP connections use to reach MCP servers, and the sandbox the codemode tool runs scripts in. Each is also its own provider.

parts.name: Pi Schema and Pi Telemetry libraries
parts.why: Reach Pi only inside Pi AI and Pi Agent Core: tool-argument validation and request spans. Each is also its own provider.

parts.name: Configuration and utilities
parts.why: Paths, start-up migrations, HTTP and stdout plumbing, helpers (src/config.ts, src/migrations.ts, src/utils/, src/core/http-dispatcher.ts): how parts reach the file system and network.

parts.name: Documentation and examples
parts.why: The user guides, references and example extensions and SDK programs (docs/, examples/): surfaces consumers read as part of the product.

components.name: Agent session
components.description: Runs a conversation in one working folder and keeps it as a session: prompts and queues, retries, compaction, model and tool choice, branching, export and sharing.

parts.name: Session store
parts.why: Storage of the session tree (src/core/session-manager.ts); the session runtime copies imported files into the session folder and the terminal UI deletes session files, so it is not the only writer and stays inside this component.

parts.name: Session runtime
parts.why: Replaces the session on new, resume, fork and import (src/core/agent-session-runtime.ts); works on the same sessions.

parts.name: Compaction and branch summaries
parts.why: Decide cut points and write summaries but keep nothing (src/core/compaction/, "Compaction and summarization utilities"): the result counts only once the session appends it, the session decides when to compact and whether to take an extension's session_before_compact result instead, and AgentSession's header lists compaction among what it encapsulates. A step of Compact session and Branch session.

parts.name: Session wiring
parts.why: The dependency-injection setup that builds the session and its services (src/core/sdk.ts, agent-session-services.ts).

parts.name: System prompt, messages, cache warmer, usage
parts.why: Steps of a run on the same session state (system-prompt.ts, messages.ts, cache-warmer.ts, usage-totals.ts, cache-stats.ts, nested-tool-calls.ts); nested tool calls are recorded on the parent call's result, and cache warming is provider behaviour.

parts.name: Built-in tools, codemode tool, tool search
parts.why: Variants of the tool contract that the agent loop runs and the session chooses (src/core/tools/, src/extensions/codemode, src/extensions/tool-search): adapters to the working folder and the shell that keep no state of their own. Codemode's stored values are session entries it appends, and tool_search changes the session's active tools.

parts.name: Shell command runner and exec helper
parts.why: Adapters to the shell for ! commands and for pi.exec (src/core/bash-executor.ts, exec.ts).

parts.name: Export, share and bug report
parts.why: Representations of the session and their uploads (src/core/export-html/, session-export.ts, bug-report.ts, src/modes/interactive/session-share.ts); they sit partly in the interactive mode's folder but work on the session.

components.name: Model runtime
components.description: Decides which models Pi offers, from the built-in providers, models.json, extension providers, the pi.dev catalog and virtual models, and sends each request to Pi AI.

parts.name: Model registry
parts.why: A facade that only passes calls on to the runtime (src/core/model-registry.ts), handed to extensions as ctx.modelRegistry.

parts.name: Provider composition and models.json
parts.why: Builds the provider set the runtime holds (provider-composer.ts, model-config.ts).

parts.name: pi.dev catalog overlay
parts.why: An adapter to pi.dev that wraps a provider (remote-catalog-provider.ts).

parts.name: Credential and model-list stores
parts.why: File storage Pi AI writes through (auth-storage.ts implements CredentialStore; models-store.ts implements ModelsStore).

parts.name: Virtual models
parts.why: Dispatch to the router an extension registers and change the same provider set (virtual-models.ts).

parts.name: Model pattern matching
parts.why: Steps of choosing a model from --model and --models patterns (model-resolver.ts).

parts.name: llama.cpp support
parts.why: A model provider registered through the extension API plus the /llama screen that presents the router's own model management (src/extensions/llama).

components.name: Extension runtime
components.description: Loads extensions, keeps what they register, delivers session events to their handlers and combines the answers, and passes their requests on to the session.

parts.name: Loader
parts.why: Loads modules and maps the host packages, filling the registrations the runner reads (src/core/extensions/loader.ts).

parts.name: Runner
parts.why: Dispatches events and combines results over the same registrations (src/core/extensions/runner.ts).

parts.name: Extension contract
parts.why: The ExtensionAPI and ExtensionContext types (src/core/extensions/types.ts): the contract behind the extension API interface, not a part with behaviour.

parts.name: MCP server registrations
parts.why: "The core only validates and stores registrations" (src/core/mcp-servers.ts); the MCP connections component connects them.

parts.name: Event bus
parts.why: A channel extensions share (src/core/event-bus.ts).

parts.name: Built-in extension list
parts.why: The code that registers the built-in extensions, llama.cpp, codemode, tool search and MCP, the last three replaceable by an extension that registers the same tool or command (src/extensions/index.ts).

components.name: Resource loader
components.description: Finds and loads the context files, system prompt files, skills, prompt templates, themes and extensions that apply to a working folder, in order of precedence.

parts.name: Skill and prompt-template loaders
parts.why: Parsers whose results only the loader holds (skills.ts, prompt-templates.ts).

parts.name: Package manifest reader and source info
parts.why: Read the `pi` key of package.json and label where each resource came from (pi-manifest.ts, source-info.ts).

parts.name: Slash command list
parts.why: The built-in command names and the commands resources add (slash-commands.ts): data the loader and the interfaces read.

components.name: Project trust
components.description: Decides whether a working folder may load its own settings, MCP servers, extensions and other resources, and keeps the saved decisions.

parts.name: Trust store and trust resolution
parts.why: ProjectTrustStore (trust-manager.ts) and resolveProjectTrusted (project-trust.ts) work on the same decisions in trust.json.

components.name: Package manager
components.description: Installs, updates and removes Pi packages from npm, git or local paths, and records them in settings.

parts.name: npm and git handling
parts.why: Steps of install and update inside DefaultPackageManager (package-manager.ts).

parts.name: Resource discovery and filters
parts.why: Helpers of resolve() in the same file that find a package's or folder's extensions, skills, prompts and themes and apply its filters (collect*Entries, applyPatterns in package-manager.ts).

components.name: MCP connections
components.description: Connects the MCP servers in mcp.json and those extensions register, signs in to them, and offers their tools and resources to the model.

parts.name: Connection manager
parts.why: The component's core: holds the server records, connects servers, registers their tools and decides exposure and start-up waits (src/extensions/mcp/index.ts).

parts.name: Server connections
parts.why: "The part of the MCP integration that talks to servers" (src/extensions/mcp/runtime.ts, runtime.lazy.ts): the adapter, through pi-mcp, whose connection state is a property of the manager's server records.

parts.name: Config
parts.why: Reads and edits mcp.json for the manager (config.ts, src/core/radius-mcp.ts).

parts.name: OAuth
parts.why: Sign-in state of the same servers in mcp-auth.json (oauth.ts).

parts.name: Tools, resources and log
parts.why: Steps of calling the same connections (tools.ts, resources.ts, log.ts).

parts.name: /mcp screen and pi mcp commands
parts.why: Present the manager (ui.ts, cli.ts): parts of the terminal UI and shell-command interfaces.

providers.name: Pi AI
providers.description: The pi-ai library: one API to chat with, generate images with and classify through many model providers, with their model catalogs and sign-in.

parts.name: Models collection
parts.why: Holds the provider set, alone writes credentials (login, logout and OAuth refresh inside the credential store's modify) and stored model lists, and routes each request to the provider that owns the model with its auth applied (src/models.ts, src/auth/resolve.ts); the only part that passes, so the library is not opened.

parts.name: Provider factories
parts.why: Variants of the Provider contract, each an adapter to an outside model service with its catalog, auth semantics and stream behaviour (src/providers/). They hold no record only they change: Models persists a dynamic provider's model list before running its update, and runs its OAuth refresh inside Models' own credential write.

parts.name: API implementations
parts.why: Wire-protocol adapters shared by providers (src/api/).

parts.name: Auth and OAuth flows
parts.why: Each provider's sign-in and refresh flows (src/auth/oauth/), whose credentials the Models collection stores; the credential store is storage the host supplies (src/auth/credential-store.ts).

parts.name: Model catalog
parts.why: Generated model data and the store contract for refreshed lists (src/models.generated.ts, src/providers/*.models.ts, src/model-catalog.ts, src/models-store.ts).

parts.name: Cache-warming policy
parts.why: Stateless numbers for hosts that warm prompt caches (src/cache-warming.ts: "Hosts own the scheduling; this module owns the numbers"); it serves no capability, since cache warming is provider behaviour.

parts.name: Utilities and telemetry schema
parts.why: Event streams, tool-argument validation through pi-schema, transcript helpers, environment key lookup, a registry of session clean-up callbacks and request spans through pi-telemetry (src/utils/, src/env-api-keys.ts, src/session-resources.ts, src/telemetry.ts).

parts.name: Faux provider
parts.why: A scripted provider for tests (src/providers/faux.ts): test help offered to library users.

parts.name: Entry modules
parts.why: Export surfaces (src/index.ts, oauth.ts, lazy-oauth.ts, bun-oauth.ts, bedrock-provider.ts, lazy-bedrock-provider.ts); check-entry-graphs budgets what ./models and ./utils/* may reach.

parts.name: pi-ai command line
parts.why: `pi-ai login` and `list` (src/cli.ts): a client of the Models collection, part of the pi-ai command line interface.

parts.name: Catalog generator
parts.why: Builds the model catalog from upstream sources (catalog/, scripts/): engineering tooling.

providers.name: Pi Agent Core
providers.description: The pi-agent-core library: a stateful agent that runs model turns with tool calls, queued messages and events, on a stream function the host supplies.

parts.name: Shared types
parts.why: The contract types both components use, such as AgentState, AgentLoopConfig, AgentTool and AgentEvent, and the package entry (src/types.ts, src/index.ts).

parts.name: Default stream function
parts.why: Wiring: a slot the host fills with the function that reaches a model, read by both components when none is given (src/stream-fn.ts).

parts.name: mcp-codemode example
parts.why: Documentation: an example program that wraps MCP tools and a codemode tool as agent tools (examples/mcp-codemode/).

components.name: Stateful agent
components.description: The Agent class: keeps the transcript, model, thinking level, tools and the steering and follow-up queues, and records each run's events in that state.

parts.name: Pending message queues
parts.why: Part of the agent's own state (PendingMessageQueue in src/agent.ts), changed through steer, followUp and the clear methods and drained when the loop polls.

parts.name: Event reduction
parts.why: The step that records each loop event in the same state (processEvents in src/agent.ts).

components.name: Agent loop
components.description: The low-level loop that runs one prompt or continuation turn by turn: it calls the model, runs the tool calls, takes queued messages and decides when the run ends.

parts.name: Tool-call pipeline
parts.why: Argument validation, the before and after hooks and the result of each tool call (executeToolCalls, prepareToolCall, executePreparedToolCall, runToolCall in src/agent-loop.ts); the run flow calls these unexported steps directly, on the same run.

parts.name: Model call and tool-change declarations
parts.why: Steps of each turn: streaming the assistant response and declaring changes to the tool set as system messages (streamAssistantResponse, declareToolChanges).

parts.name: Proxy stream
parts.why: A stream function that sends model requests to the application's own server (src/proxy.ts): an adapter.

providers.name: Pi TUI
providers.description: The pi-tui library: a terminal UI framework that draws components with differential rendering and handles keys, paste and mouse input.

parts.name: Renderers and built-in components
parts.why: The main and alternate screen renderers (src/tui.ts, tui-main-screen.ts, tui-alt-screen.ts, layout.ts) and the text, editor, input, Markdown, select list, image and other components (src/components/, editor-component.ts) are one tree on one Component contract: the TUI is itself its root container (TuiBase extends Container) and its setFocus writes the components' focused flag, so they change each other's records. The only part that could pass, so the library is not opened.

parts.name: Terminal input and output
parts.why: Adapters to the terminal: keys, stdin buffering, images, colours (src/terminal.ts, stdin-buffer.ts, keys.ts, terminal-image.ts, terminal-colors.ts).

parts.name: Keybindings
parts.why: A store of key settings the components read (src/keybindings.ts).

parts.name: Autocomplete, fuzzy matching, LaTeX and utilities
parts.why: Helpers of the components, autocomplete providers being variants the editor uses (src/autocomplete.ts, fuzzy.ts, colors.ts, latex.ts, utils.ts, kill-ring.ts, undo-stack.ts).

parts.name: Native clipboard helpers
parts.why: Adapters to the operating system's clipboard (native/).

providers.name: Pi MCP
providers.description: The pi-mcp library: a standalone Model Context Protocol client over stdio and Streamable HTTP, with OAuth sign-in.

parts.name: Config validation, naming and content conversion
parts.why: Helpers for applications that keep nothing (src/config.ts, naming.ts, input-schema.ts, model-content.ts, output-limit.ts, result-schema.ts), the package entry (src/index.ts) and the testing entry (src/testing/).

parts.name: AuthProvider contract
parts.why: The interface between the Streamable HTTP transport and MCP OAuth (src/auth-provider.ts), not a part with behaviour.

components.name: MCP client
components.description: McpClient with its transports: connects to one MCP server, keeps the connection, and sends the protocol's requests with correlation, timeouts and cancellation.

parts.name: Protocol types and JSON-RPC helpers
parts.why: Message types and helpers of the same client (src/protocol/).

parts.name: Transports
parts.why: Variants of the transport contract, stdio, Streamable HTTP, pipe and in-memory (src/transports/): adapters that own framing and I/O.

components.name: MCP OAuth
components.description: pi-mcp's OAuth client: signs in to an MCP server's authorization server, keeps the tokens and client registration in a store the application supplies, and refreshes them for connections.

parts.name: Authorization flow and discovery
parts.why: Steps on the same sign-in state: metadata discovery, client registration, PKCE, token exchange, refresh and step-up (src/oauth/flow.ts, discovery.ts, client-settings.ts).

parts.name: Sign-in halves
parts.why: startMcpSignIn and completeMcpSignIn save to the same store as the OAuth provider (src/oauth/sign-in.ts).

parts.name: Callback servers
parts.why: Local HTTP listeners that receive the browser's redirect (src/oauth/callback.ts, loopback.ts): adapters.

providers.name: Pi Codemode
providers.description: The pi-codemode library: runs model-written JavaScript in a QuickJS sandbox whose only capability is calling the tools it is given.

parts.name: Sandboxes
parts.why: CodemodeSandbox, RemoteCodemodeSandbox and InlineCodemodeSandbox "share one API, one script environment, and one result format" and "share the same host side, prelude, and VM, and replace only the worker thread" (README; CodemodeSandboxBase in src/runtime/execution.ts): one part with variants, the only one that could pass.

parts.name: QuickJS runtime, worker and Cloudflare Durable Object
parts.why: Where a variant runs the VM (src/runtime/vm.ts, prelude-source.ts, worker.ts, protocol.ts, src/wasm.ts, src/cloudflare.ts): an implementation choice whose isolation carries one run of the sandbox's own capability and persists nothing.

parts.name: Source format and declarations
parts.why: Parse the options line and generate tool declarations (src/source.ts, src/declarations.ts, src/identifier.ts).

providers.name: Pi Schema
providers.description: The pi-schema library: JSON Schema builders and a validator that compiles a schema into plain checks without eval.

parts.name: Compiler and validator
parts.why: Decide whether a value matches a schema (src/compiler.ts, validator.ts, checks.ts, coerce.ts, resolver.ts, explain.ts, shared.ts): the only deciding part, so the library is not opened.

parts.name: Format checks
parts.why: A group with its own entry-point rule in check-entry-graphs (src/formats/, loaded only through ./formats), but pure checks the compiler calls through compile()'s formats option: steps of the same decision.

parts.name: Builders and types
parts.why: Return plain JSON Schema objects and their static types and decide nothing (src/builders.ts, annotations.ts, types.ts, typebox-static.ts, index.ts).

providers.name: Pi Telemetry
providers.description: The pi-telemetry library: a vendor-neutral contract for spans and metrics that Pi's packages report to, with no-op and in-memory reference adapters.

parts.name: Contract and reference adapters
parts.why: The context, span and metric contract with its no-op and in-memory variants (src/index.ts, noop.ts, memory.ts, metrics.ts; InMemoryTelemetryContext implements TelemetryContext and TelemetryStore): one part with variants, and no exporter.

parts.name: Typed schemas
parts.why: Typed span starters and metrics that wrap a context and pass calls on (createTypedSpanStarter in src/index.ts, createTypedMetrics in src/metrics.ts).

parts.name: Render and conformance suite
parts.why: A text representation of recorded spans (src/render.ts) and test help for adapter authors (src/testing/).

outsideServices.name: AI model providers
outsideServices.description: The model services Pi AI calls: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Amazon Bedrock, Azure, OpenRouter, GitHub Copilot, the Radius gateway, a llama.cpp router and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, among about forty.

outsideServices.name: MCP servers
outsideServices.description: Model Context Protocol servers the user configures or an extension registers, local over stdio or remote over Streamable HTTP, including the Radius MCP server.

outsideServices.name: Radius
outsideServices.description: Earendil Works' service for Pi at radius.pi.dev; Pi uploads shared sessions and bug reports to it (its model gateway and MCP server are reached as one of the AI model providers and MCP servers).

outsideServices.name: GitHub
outsideServices.description: GitHub gists, reached through the `gh` command, where /share puts a session when Radius is not used.

outsideServices.name: Package sources
outsideServices.description: The npm registry and git hosts Pi packages are installed from.

outsideServices.name: pi.dev
outsideServices.description: Pi's website, which serves the current model catalog per provider.

outsideServices.name: llama.cpp router
outsideServices.description: A local llama.cpp server in router mode that discovers GGUF models and loads them on demand; Pi manages its models here, and Pi AI sends it chat requests as one of the AI model providers.

outsideServices.name: Hugging Face
outsideServices.description: The Hugging Face Hub, searched for GGUF models the llama.cpp router can download.

resources.name: Session
resources.description: A saved conversation in a working folder: messages, tool calls and results, model changes and compactions, stored as a tree of branches.

resources.name: Model
resources.description: A model Pi can use through a provider: a chat, image or classifier model, built in, configured in models.json, added by an extension, or virtual.

resources.name: Model response
resources.description: What a model returns for one request: text, thinking and tool calls, generated images, or classifier answers.

resources.name: Provider credential
resources.description: An API key or account sign-in for a model provider, saved in auth.json or taken from the environment.

resources.name: Pi package
resources.description: An npm, git or local package of extensions, skills, prompt templates and themes, declared in user or project settings.

resources.name: Skill
resources.description: A folder with a SKILL.md and supporting files that the model loads when a task calls for it, also available as /skill:name.

resources.name: Prompt template
resources.description: A Markdown prompt available as a slash command, with arguments.

resources.name: Theme
resources.description: A set of terminal colours for Pi's interface.

resources.name: Context file
resources.description: Instructions Pi adds to the system prompt: AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md in the folder, its parents and the agent directory, and SYSTEM.md or APPEND_SYSTEM.md.

resources.name: Extension
resources.description: A TypeScript module loaded into Pi, with the handlers and items it registers.

resources.name: Tool
resources.description: Something the model can call: a built-in tool such as read, bash, edit or write, an extension's tool, or an MCP tool.

resources.name: Command
resources.description: A slash command, keyboard shortcut or command-line flag that an extension adds.

resources.name: MCP server
resources.description: An MCP server Pi connects to, configured in mcp.json or registered by an extension.

resources.name: Project trust decision
resources.description: Whether a working folder may load its own settings and resources, saved per folder in trust.json.

resources.name: Settings
resources.description: The user's and project's saved preferences: default model and tools, compaction, retries, display, keybindings.

resources.name: Dialog
resources.description: A question an extension shows the user (select, confirm, input or editor), open until answered or cancelled.

resources.name: Widget
resources.description: Something an extension shows in Pi's terminal: a widget, status entry, header, footer, custom editor, custom screen or message renderer.

resources.name: Agent
resources.description: A stateful agent in pi-agent-core: its transcript, model, thinking level, tools and queued messages.

resources.name: Agent run
resources.description: One run of pi-agent-core's agent loop, from a prompt or a continuation until the model stops calling tools and no queued message is left: its turns, the assistant messages and tool results it adds, and its events.

resources.name: Component
resources.description: A piece of a terminal interface built with pi-tui: text, editor, input, Markdown, select list, image, box or a custom one.

resources.name: MCP connection
resources.description: A client connected to one MCP server, with its negotiated protocol version and session.

resources.name: MCP tool
resources.description: A tool an MCP server offers, with its input and output schemas and annotations.

resources.name: MCP resource
resources.description: A document or file an MCP server offers by URI, listed directly or through URI templates.

resources.name: MCP sign-in
resources.description: An OAuth authorization with an MCP server's authorization server: client registration and tokens.

resources.name: Sandbox
resources.description: A configured place where model-written scripts run, with the tools and globals it gives them and its limits.

resources.name: Script run
resources.description: One run of a script in a sandbox: its output, return value or error, the tool calls it made and its store writes.

resources.name: Schema
resources.description: A JSON Schema, built with the builders or supplied as is, compiled into a check.

resources.name: Span
resources.description: A timed record of one operation, with attributes, events, status and links.

resources.name: Metric
resources.description: A counter, up-down counter or histogram with typed attributes.

resources.name: Artifact
resources.description: An item shared on Radius, here a session, with a viewer link visible to the user's organization.

resources.name: Bug report
resources.description: A report to Pi's developers with a transcript or summary, environment and provider configuration without secrets, and error diagnostics.

resources.name: Gist
resources.description: A private GitHub gist holding a session export.

resources.name: Package release
resources.description: A published version of an npm package, or a git branch, tag or commit.

resources.name: Model catalog
resources.description: The published list of a provider's models with capabilities, limits and prices.

resources.name: Local model
resources.description: A GGUF model the llama.cpp router knows, downloaded, loading, loaded or unloaded.

resources.name: Hub model
resources.description: A model repository on the Hugging Face Hub with its GGUF files.

interfaces.description: The @earendil-works/pi-ai npm package and its entry points.

interfaces.description: The `pi-ai` command: login and list providers.

interfaces.name: pi-agent-core package
interfaces.description: The @earendil-works/pi-agent-core npm package: the Agent class and the low-level agent loop.

interfaces.name: pi-tui package
interfaces.description: The @earendil-works/pi-tui npm package.

interfaces.name: pi-mcp package
interfaces.description: The @earendil-works/pi-mcp npm package and its oauth and testing entry points.

interfaces.description: The @earendil-works/pi-codemode npm package and its portable, cloudflare, source and declarations entry points.

questions.question: Are Pi's published libraries their own providers, or interfaces of one provider, Pi?
questions.answer: Seven providers (Pi AI, Pi Agent Core, Pi TUI, Pi MCP, Pi Codemode, Pi Schema, Pi Telemetry) rather than one Pi provider with the libraries as interfaces; each is a separate npm package with its own README and users who never run the coding agent, but they ship from one repository with one version, so the rule on separate products does not settle it.

questions.question: How does a library that is a Level 1 provider appear inside Pi?
questions.answer: Pi AI and Pi Agent Core are named in Pi's sharedComponents, since each passes the component test inside Pi, rather than defining a second Model access or Agent loop component; Pi TUI, Pi MCP and Pi Codemode stay libraries inside Pi, because there they only draw, reach MCP servers or run scripts for a component.

questions.question: Are the tools (read, bash, edit, write, codemode, tool search) a component?
questions.answer: Parts of the Agent session rather than a Tools component with variants; they fulfil one contract and keep no state of their own, but codemode and tool search are separately registered built-in extensions, so either reading fits.

questions.question: Is the session store a component of its own?
questions.answer: Part of the Agent session rather than a Session store component; SessionManager makes real decisions (the active branch, the model context), but the session runtime and the terminal UI also write and delete session files, and parts that change each other's records are one component.

questions.question: Is MCP support a component while codemode and tool search are not?
questions.answer: MCP connections is a component and codemode and tool search are tools, rather than treating all built-in extensions alike; MCP keeps its own state (mcp.json edits, mcp-auth.json, live connections), while the other two keep none outside the session.

questions.question: Is project trust part of the resource loader?
questions.answer: Its own component rather than part of the Resource loader; it keeps trust.json and decides trust, and is read by start-up, package commands and MCP config as well as the loader.

questions.question: Is Radius one outside service or three?
questions.answer: One Radius service for shared sessions and bug reports, with its model gateway listed among the AI model providers and its MCP server among the MCP servers, rather than one Radius service serving all three; Pi reaches the gateway and the MCP server through the same code as any other provider or server.

questions.question: Are settings a resource?
questions.answer: A Settings resource for Change settings rather than leaving /settings out; the model warns that a setting is not a resource, but users open, scope (user or project) and edit their settings as one thing, and dropping it would leave /settings without a place.

questions.question: Who consumes print mode and JSON mode?
questions.answer: Print mode on the Pi user's boundary (their own scripts) and JSON mode on the Integrator's, rather than both on one; the docs offer both for scripts, and JSON mode's structured events serve programs that follow a run.

questions.question: What resources do extension dialogs and widgets work on?
questions.answer: Dialog and Widget resources rather than modelling them as interactions of the terminal UI; dialogs have IDs and an answer or cancellation over RPC, and widgets are set and cleared by key.

questions.question: Where does llama.cpp support sit?
questions.answer: In the Model runtime rather than as its own component; it registers a model provider and presents the router's own model management, keeping no state the router does not hold.

questions.question: Is self-update (`pi update` for Pi itself) a capability?
questions.answer: Excluded as setting up the system rather than a Pi user capability; it changes the installed Pi, not what the user works with, though users run it from the same command line.

questions.question: How are the imports that cross between Pi's components settled, since nothing in the coding agent enforces its inner seams?
questions.answer: Accepted as uses of a component's exported functions and shared helpers rather than redrawing the components: the session calls model-resolver.ts and virtual-models.ts helpers next to ModelRuntime, and prompt-templates.ts and skills.ts functions on resources it got through ResourceLoader; MCP connections imports text helpers from the session's tools (truncate.ts, render-utils.ts), the codemode and tool_search tool names, and auth-storage.ts's file-locking backend for its own mcp-auth.json; the extension runner builds ctx.getSystemPrompt with the session's system-prompt.ts; the package manager reads manifests with the loader's pi-manifest.ts; src/extensions/index.ts is the registry of built-in extensions. Three reach past a contract and are left as they are: the terminal UI deletes a cancelled fork's session file itself (interactive-mode.ts), the Radius login in the shell commands and the terminal UI writes mcp.json through MCP connections' config.ts rather than through the extension API (shell commands do not load extensions), and the session, the extension runner and the resource loader import the terminal UI's theme module. The coding agent has no internal boundary check, so no rule settles which of these to treat as defects.

questions.question: Are the Agent and the agent loop one part of Pi Agent Core? (changed in the deepening run)
questions.answer: Two components, Stateful agent and Agent loop, rather than the one part the earlier map had; the code contradicts its reason that the loop runs turns on the Agent's state: the Agent hands the loop a copy of its transcript and tools (createContextSnapshot) and alone writes its state from the loop's events (processEvents), while the loop alone decides each turn on its own working context, imports nothing from agent.ts and is offered without the Agent class (README, Low-Level API). The component rule speaks of state or decisions, and the loop holds only a run in progress, so the rule alone does not settle it.

questions.question: Is pi-mcp's OAuth a step of connecting or a component of Pi MCP? (changed in the deepening run)
questions.answer: A component, MCP OAuth, beside MCP client, rather than sign-in steps of a connection as the earlier map had it; the code contradicts that reading: sign-in runs on its own behind the ./oauth entry (startMcpSignIn, completeMcpSignIn, authorizeMcp), only src/oauth saves the sign-in state, through the McpOAuthStateStore the application injects, the HTTP transport reaches it only through AuthProvider, and it changed alone in 11 of its 14 commits since May. No rule says whether a part that talks to an outside authorization server is an adapter; it counts as a component because the sign-in state and its refresh are its own. src/oauth imports only a protocol version constant and an object guard from the client's protocol folder, accepted as shared helpers.

questions.question: Does pi-mcp's OAuth pass the component test inside Pi as well, now that it is a component of Pi MCP?
questions.answer: No: Pi MCP stays a library inside Pi, as the earlier answer on libraries inside Pi has it, rather than its OAuth becoming a shared component of MCP connections; inside Pi, MCP connections' own store also changes the sign-in records (McpOAuthCredentialStore.remove on sign-out, load taking over legacy keys, src/extensions/mcp/oauth.ts), so the two change each other's records, while a standalone application only supplies the store. The rule applies the same way in both places; what differs is the code around the library.

questions.question: Is compaction a component of the Agent session?
questions.answer: Part of the Agent session rather than a Compaction component; compaction/ decides cut points and writes summaries, but it keeps nothing, its result counts only once the session appends it, the session decides when to compact and whether to take an extension's session_before_compact result instead, and AgentSession's header lists compaction among what it encapsulates. The agent loop is also stateless yet a component, because library developers run agents with it without the Agent class and it holds the run's working context; no rule says when a stateless part that decides is a component, so the two could also be read alike.

questions.question: What resource does the agent loop work on?
questions.answer: A new resource, Agent run, rather than the Agent; the loop works on a copy of the transcript and produces messages the Agent records afterwards, so its contract does not work on the Agent directly, though a developer may think of a run as part of the agent.

questions.question: Is runToolCall, which the Agent session calls for nested tool calls, its own capability on the Agent session's boundary with Pi Agent Core?
questions.answer: A step of Run prompt rather than a capability Run tool call, so that Level 2 boundary keeps its four capabilities; the session calls it only while a tool call of the current run executes (codemode's nested calls, src/core/nested-tool-calls.ts) and records the result on that call's tool result, but the session could also be read as wanting the nested result for itself.

questions.question: Is MCP OAuth's access token a capability for the MCP client or a step of each request?
questions.answer: A capability, Get access token, with onUnauthorized() as its step, rather than a step of the client's requests to servers; token() is the operation the AuthProvider contract exists for, as the earlier map's Get provider credential is for MCP connections, but the transport calls it only so its requests to the server succeed, and the look-alike test does not say whether that counts as wanting it for itself.
